// diagnostic

E-ERR-SIGIL

`T ! E` and `T ? E` are retired infix fallible type spellings.

What

`T ! E` and `T ? E` are retired infix fallible type spellings.

Why

The success type and error type have one unambiguous prefix contract, so `?` keeps one meaning: possible absence when it prefixes a success type.

Fix

Write `?Entry !StoreError`, `Int !(DbError | TimeoutError)`, or `!IOError`; remove a bare `!` contract because failure is implicit.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E-ERR-SIGIL: tests/ui/retired_fallible_type_sigil.stderr.
